title: Web Design Portfolio Roast: What Actually Gets You Hired in 2024/2025
transcript:
I have reviewed thousands of portfolios, and here is the brutal truth: clients and employers do not buy code or Figma screens; they buy outcomes and problem-solving.
A gallery of finished screenshots is NOT a case study. A real case study follows the PSR framework: Problem, Solution, Result.
Section 1: The Problem & Context. What was broken? Who was the client? What were the business constraints?
Section 2: Your Specific Role. If it was a team project, say exactly what you did. Did you design the design system? Did you optimize database queries? Did you build the checkout flow?
Section 3: The Process & Key Decisions. Show wireframes, trade-offs, and pivot points. Show that you think like a senior designer or engineer.
Section 4: The Measurable Impact. 'Increased checkout conversion by 14%', 'Reduced LCP from 4.2s to 0.8s', 'Handled 50,000 concurrent users'. Numbers create instant credibility.
Include 3 to 5 deep case studies instead of 12 shallow projects. If you have bad projects on your site, they drag down the perceived quality of your best work.
